recipes.name: Kitchiri - Herati Afghan Rice
ingredients: ½ cup dry split mung beans
instructions: After an overnight soak, much of the skin separates from the mung beans. Traditionally, the skin is scooped out before cooking, but this is optional. Rinse and drain both the mung beans and rice.
Drizzle the oil in a large pot over medium heat. When hot, add the onions and cook until very deeply golden brown, about 15 minutes.
Then add the drained mung beans, increase the heat to medium-high, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes to lightly toast. Stir often.
Add the spices and cook for 1 more minute, stirring throughout.
Add the water and cook for 3 minutes, or until boiling.
Add the rice and cover it with enough water so that the water is about ½ inch (2 cm) above the rice*. Bring to a boil, partially cover, reduce to a gentle simmer, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes.
To make the garlic yogurt sauce, combine the yogurt, garlic, and salt in a small bowl. Set aside until ready to serve.
Mix the cooked rice to fluff it, then use the end of a wooden spatula to create 5 holes in the rice.
Taste test. If the rice is not yet cooked, add a small splash of water. Then wrap the lid of the pot with a clean dish towel and place this over the pot. Let sit for 5 to 7 minutes over low heat.
To serve, top the rice with a drizzle of the garlic yogurt sauce. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Find split mung beans at your local Persian grocery store. You can use whole mung beans instead as well, but they should be soaked overnight and then cooked in the boiling water for 8 - 10 minutes before the rice is added, to ensure that the rice and beans are done cooking at the same time. When the soaked mung beans are rinsed, the skins should come off. * Careful to not add too much water, as more water can always be added later.
Storage Keep the kitchari separate from the garlic yogurt in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
